title: Field Claim
summary: Stake out fields with a determinant: place a post for a given area, make three posts collinear, and find the line through two beacons.
subject: mathematics
concepts: Area of a triangle by a determinant
Equation of a line through two points
learningOutcome: The student can find an unknown vertex from a given area (taking both signs), decide when three points are collinear, and write the equation of the line through two points from a determinant.

levels.title: The deed’s area
levels.adds: Baseline: area = ½|x₁(y₂ − y₃) + x₂(y₃ − y₁) + x₃(y₁ − y₂)|, and the absolute value gives two possible posts (Ex 4.2 Q1, Q3, Q5; Example 7).
hints: Write the determinant with the unknown k in it.
Set ½|…| equal to the deed’s area, then remove the absolute value with ±.
Two values of k solve it; the deed says which side of the gate is allowed.

levels.title: A straight rope
levels.adds: New: three points are collinear when the determinant (so the area) is zero (Ex 4.2 Q2).
hints: The area of three collinear points is zero.
Put the unknown coordinate into the determinant and set it equal to 0.
It gives a linear equation in the unknown.

levels.title: Line through two beacons
levels.adds: New: the determinant of (x, y, 1) and the two beacons being zero is the equation of the line (Ex 4.2 Q4).
hints: A point (x, y) is on the line when the determinant with the two beacons is 0.
Expand along the first row and collect x, y and the constant.

misconceptions: The area from a determinant can be negative
A given area fixes the third vertex uniquely
Collinear points make a triangle of small area
